Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players stride out to the middle. Muneeba Ali and Sidra Ameen are the openers for Pakistan Women. Jess Kerr to start with the ball. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then! 266 is what Pakistan Women have in front of them and for a side that has struggled with the bat, they will have to play out of their skins to chase this down. New Zealand Women will feel they have got enough runs on the board and would be confident of defending this total. Stay tuned to see how the chase unfolds.

Suzie Bates is up for a quick chat. She says it has been a tough tournament for the team and for herself personally. Mentions, she just aimed to apply herself in the middle. Says, it is always nice to perform in front of an incredible crowd. Tells that she is sure there are pretty great names in the 5000-club and it would mean a lot later on. Mentions, anything above 250 seems to be handy and appreciates the effort of Martin in the death overs.

Pakistan bowlers struggled initially but Anam Amin provided the breakthrough they were looking for. They couldn't keep the run flow in check but Nida Dar struck twice in the 19th over and that brought Pakistan back in the game. The spinners bowled exceedingly well in the middle overs and did well to contain runs. The bowlers got wickets at timely intervals and did a good job to keep things tight at the back end as well. But 32 runs in the last 2 overs will definitely hurt them. They missed a couple of chances in the game and had they taken it, they could have restricted NZ to a much lower score.

New Zealand started very well and both, Sophie Devine and Suzie Bates showed some aggression straightaway. However, Devine departed soon. Suzie Bates and Amelia Kerr then stitched a nice partnership of 68 but Kerr and Amy Satterthwaite holed out in the same over and that put New Zealand in a little trouble. However, Bates kept building partnerships and notched up a sensational ton to put NZ in the driver's seat. After she got out, they started losing wickets quickly but Katey Martin played a good knock at the end as New Zealand managed to come back from a mini-collapse and put a fighting total on the board.

Pakistan did well to get wickets in cluster in the end but also leaked quite a few runs and that would hurt them. New Zealand's innings was all about Suzie Bates who scored a terrific ton and also became the first NZ batter to cross 5000 ODI runs. It is her innings and a late flourish from Katey Martin that has helped New Zealand to put up 265 on the board.

Fatima Sana is brought into the attack now.
Angled into the pads. Kerr defends it back to the bowler on the front foot. A wicket taking over of Amin comes to an end.
Flatter, on middle and leg. Bates goes back to flick it to mid-wicket for a single.

It is a short ball, outside off. Kerr cuts it to deep point on the back foot. The batters pick three runs before the fielder cuts it out. This is really good running and Kerr is off the mark instantly.
Amelia Kerr walks out to bat at No.3.

OUT! TIMBER! A huge blow for New Zealand Women. Sophie Devine holes out as she looked to be in her groove. Anam Amin draws the first blood here. It is full yet again, on the off stump. Sophie Devine shuffles across, tries to flick it away but ends up playing all around it. The ball goes through to rattle the stumps. Can Pakistan build on this wicket?
SIX! BANG! Sophie Devine taking the charge now. It is fuller, outside off. Sophie Devine shuffles across and slog-sweeps it over the square leg fence for a biggie.
Flighted, angled into the stumps. Sophie Devine blocks it back to the bowler.
On a length, on off. Bates cuts it to point.
The physio runs into the field. Diana Baig seems to be in some pain. She might've hurt her finger, as she got in the path of the shot. Will she be able to continue?
Full again, on off. Suzie Bates drives it hard back to the bowler. Diana Baig half-stops it and seems to have hurt her finger.
Full, on middle. Played to mid on.

Review! Suzie Bates takes the review with one second to spare for lbw. The on-field decision is OUT. The UltraEdge confirms no bat is involved. The Ball Tracking shows the wicket is missing. The umpire is forced to change the decision. New Zealand Women do not lose a review here.

NOT OUT! Fuller in length, coming in from middle. Suzie Bates clears her front leg and looks to flick but misses. She gets hit on the pads. Diana Baig appeal and the umpire takes a lot of time before raising his finger. Suzie Bates consults Sophie Devine and opts for the review at the last second. Nothing on UltraEdge and the Ball Tracker shows wickets missing. A good review from New Zealand Women.
FOUR! Bates is in the mood! Full and on middle, Suzie Bates advances a bit and flicks it to deep square leg. Great timing on that one and she gets a boundary.
Good-length ball, on off. Bates taps it to cover.
WIDE! Sprays this one down leg, Suzie Bates misses her flick. Wide called.
Shortish, outside off. Devine cuts it to cover.
This is worked to wide of mid on for a single.
Outside off, Bates crunches it towards covers. The fielder there does well to slide to her left and stop the ball.
Tossed up, on middle. Suzie Bates chips it back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, Sophie Devine pushes it to long off for one.
Floats it up, outside off. Devine taps it to point.
FOUR! This is good positive batting! Fuller now on the pads, Suzie Bates clears her front leg and flicks it behind square on the leg side for another boundary. Nice start from New Zealand Women.
On a length, on off. Bates pushes it to cover.
Length, on off. Bates plays it to mid off.

FOUR! Bates finds her first boundary now! Excellent shot from her blade! Length ball, on middle and leg. Suzie Bates stands tall and drives it straight down the ground. It is dead straight and the ball just races away to the fence.
Length ball, on middle. Knocked back to the bowler.
Length ball, leg-lined. Devine looks to tuck but gets hit on the pads. The ball rolls to mid-wicket for a leg bye.
Short and outside off, cut away towards covers.
Flighted ball, on middle. Bates sweeps it to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
Slower through the air, outside off. Suzie Bates chops it onto the deck.
Pushes this loopy ball to mid off to get off the strike now. A single!

FOUR! Devine gets off the mark in style. Full and on the pads, Sophie Devine latches onto that. She sweeps it to deep square leg and there is no fielder there. Gets the first boundary of the New Zealand innings.
Flatter ball, outside off. Devine pushes it to point.
Time for some early spin. Anam Amin to bowl with the second new ball from the other end.
A dot to end! Good-length ball, on middle. Suzie Bates defends it back to the bowler. A tidy start from Diana Baig. Just 2 runs off it.
Good-length ball, on off. Suzie Bates punches it to wide of mid off.
Suzie Bates and New Zealand Women get underway! Fuller, on the pads. Suzie Bates places it nicely through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Length ball, shaping away, on off. Suzie Bates pushes it to cover.
Fuller, on off. Bates drives it nicely towards mid off.
Diana Baig starts with a low full toss, swinging away, on middle. Suzie Bates plays it to mid on.

Done with all the pre-match proceedings! The Pakistan Women players now take the field. Followed by Sophie Devine and Suzie Bates who walk out to open for New Zealand Women. But before we get going, all the players unite to support the Black Lives Matter movement. Diana Baig to start with the new ball. Here we go...

The game is set to begin. Both the teams stride out to the middle, as the crowd greets them with a round of applause. All the players line-up on the field for their respective national anthems. It will be Pakistan's first, followed by the one for the hosts.

PITCH REPORT - Sanjay Manjrekar says that it is sunny out here with no clouds hovering around. Tells the side boundaries are identical and the straight boundaries are quite long. Anjum Chopra says that the script doesn't change for the seam bowlers though because it should nip around. Adds that the dry nature of the surface and the brown color will aid the spinners.

Sophie Devine, the New Zealand skipper, is in for a chat. She says, they were anyways planning to bat first. Mentions, they aim to put on a performance and entertain the crowd gathered. Ends by saying, they have a single change to their side.

Bismah Maroof, Pakistan skipper, says that they will bowl first. Mentions that there is moisture and they want to take advantage of that. Tells that it is their last game and they want to give their all. Informs they have made two changes.

New Zealand Women (Playing XI) - Suzie Bates, Sophie Devine (C), Amelia Kerr, Amy Satterthwaite, Maddy Green, Brooke Halliday, Katey Martin (WK), Frances Mackay, Hannah Rowe, Rosemary Mair (In for Lea Tahuhu), Jess Kerr.

Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Sidra Ameen, Muneeba Ali (In for Nahida Khan), Bismah Maroof (C), Omaima Sohail, Nida Dar, Aliya Riaz, Fatima Sana, Sidra Nawaz (WK), Diana Baig, Nashra Sandhu, Anam Amin (In for Aiman Anwer).
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of Pakistan Women. They have opted to BOWL first.

Pakistan Women are already knocked out of the tournament and are playing for pride. They have only managed a solitary win out of their 6 games and would want to end their campaign on a winning note. But against a side like New Zealand, they will need to play out of their skin and be at their absolute best to get something out of this fixture. Stay tuned for toss and team news.

New Zealand will need a miracle to qualify from here. First, they need to secure a win by a huge margin and then hope that India and England both lose their last league game. They are more or less on the brink of elemination but they would want to give their all and end this tournament on a high and give the home crowd something to cheer for. The home condition will certainly favor the White Ferns and are firm favourites to win this game.

Hello and a warm welcome to match 26 of the Women's World Cup where New Zealand Women will cross swords against Pakistan Women. New Zealand have had their own struggles and they are coming across a side who have had their moments in this tournament. This is their last league match and both of them are coming off a loss against England. Which team will get a win here? We shall find out.
